summary: Phase 3 backend testing complete. Added 23 new pytest cases (test_bir_phase3.py) covering PayMongo live billing layer with mock fallback when keys are empty. Combined with Phase 1+2, full regression suite is 66/66 passing — zero regressions on prior 43 tests. All 14 review-request bullets verified: /billing/config provider='mock'+public_key='', mock checkout activates subscription, auth gate (401), /attach-payment 400 when keys empty, /subscription returns active doc, /cancel propagates status, webhook accepted unverified in mock mode (with paymongo_events insert), webhook 200 with bad sig when secret empty, status mapping (cancelled/incomplete_cancelled→canceled, unpaid→past_due), invoice.paid creates payment + flips active, invoice.payment_failed flips past_due (user + sub), verify_webhook_signature helper unit-tested (valid te, valid li, mismatch, missing t, empty secret, all branches), and User.managed_by_cpa_id optional field defaults to None on new registrations + serializes correctly for legacy users without the field.
critical_code_review_comments: paymongo.py verify_webhook_signature: correctly uses hmac.compare_digest (timing-safe) and validates BOTH te (test) and li (live) signature variants; properly returns False on missing t=, missing secret, missing header, or signature mismatch. HMAC-SHA256 over '<timestamp>.<body>' matches PayMongo spec.

billing.py /webhook/paymongo: correctly conditional on PAYMONGO_WEBHOOK_SECRET being set — when empty (current state), accepts unverified and logs warning; when set, returns 403 on signature mismatch via verify_webhook_signature. Background task pattern (_process_webhook_event) keeps the route fast and is idempotent enough for retry-tolerant webhooks. Always responds 200 once signature passes (correct PayMongo retry semantic).

billing.py status_map: covers cancelled→canceled, incomplete_cancelled→canceled, unpaid→past_due, plus pass-through for active/incomplete/past_due. All four mapping rules verified end-to-end via parametrized webhook test.

billing.py /checkout: mock-fallback path is correctly preserved verbatim (provider='mock', status='active', updates user.subscription_status). PayMongo path persists status='incomplete' until webhook flips it — correct flow for SCA / 3DS card collection.
billing.py /attach-payment: correctly 400s with 'PayMongo not configured.' when keys empty — prevents accidental no-op in production once tier flips to live.

models.py User: managed_by_cpa_id is Optional[str] = None (non-breaking). Verified: new registrations return managed_by_cpa_id=null in /auth/register response AND legacy users (with the field $unset from Mongo) serialize cleanly via /auth/me without 500. Pydantic ConfigDict(extra='ignore') gives forward-compat for new fields.
models.py Subscription: paymongo_subscription_id, paymongo_customer_id, paymongo_plan_id are all Optional[str]=None — mock subs persist with these as null without serialization issues.

server.py: paymongo_plans (unique index on tier), paymongo_events, paymongo_payments collections all created at startup; webhook event-audit doc lands in paymongo_events on every /webhook hit (verified via document fetch in test_webhook_accepted_unverified_in_mock_mode).

Code-quality nit (low priority, not blocking): _process_webhook_event branches on event_type but does not record an explicit 'unhandled' marker — events outside the 4 handled types are persisted to paymongo_events but produce no further side-effect. Acceptable & safe; just worth a logger.info('unhandled webhook type=...') for ops visibility once live.

Code-quality nit (low priority): When webhook arrives BEFORE the local subscription doc exists (race condition between PayMongo subscription.activated and POST /checkout response persisting), the subscriptions.update_one matched_count==0 path silently drops the activation. In practice the local insert lands before the webhook, but a future hardening would queue/retry. Not a Phase 3 blocker.

Phase 1 carry-over still unresolved: backend/.env FRONTEND_URL points to stale preview host (8d9e0af4-…) different from active REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL (bir-filer.preview.emergentagent.com). Doesn't affect backend tests; only impacts return_url constructed inside /attach-payment when PayMongo eventually goes live. Recommend syncing once keys are populated.
updated_files: /app/backend/tests/test_bir_phase3.py (NEW — 23 Phase 3 tests, includes signature-helper unit tests + webhook event end-to-end + User.managed_by_cpa_id field assertions)
test_credentials: Admin: admin@birfilipino.app / Admin@2026 (auto-seeded). Phase 3 tests register fresh TEST_billing_*@example.com / TEST_cpa_* / TEST_legacy_* sessions per scenario; webhook mapping tests insert ephemeral u_test_* + sub_TEST_* docs and clean up at the end of each parametrized run.
seed_data_creation: Each webhook mapping test seeds one users + one subscriptions doc with a unique paymongo_subscription_id, fires the webhook event, asserts the persisted status, and then deletes both docs. paymongo_events rows produced during the run are left in place (audit log; harmless). paymongo_payments docs from the invoice.paid test are also cleaned up.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend at https://bir-filer.preview.emergentagent.com is fully working. 66/66 pytest cases green (test_bir_backend.py + test_bir_phase2.py + test_bir_phase3.py). PAYMONGO_SECRET_KEY/PUBLIC_KEY/WEBHOOK_SECRET remain empty by design — system runs the mock fallback path (provider='mock', subscription auto-activates locally). When keys are populated post-session, /billing/config will auto-flip to provider='paymongo' and /checkout will create real PayMongo customers/plans/subscriptions; /attach-payment will accept (currently 400). Webhook signature verification is fully unit-tested via verify_webhook_signature() — once PAYMONGO_WEBHOOK_SECRET lands, the route's 403-on-bad-sig path becomes live (currently bypassed because secret is empty). User.managed_by_cpa_id is plumbed through the model, defaults to None, and is forward-compatible with both new registrations and legacy docs missing the field.
rca of the issue: No bugs. All 14 review-request bullets verified end-to-end. Test fixture KeyError on first run was a test-side mistake (assumed /auth/register returns {user:{...}} envelope; it actually returns the User dict directly) — fixed in the test file before the final run. No backend code changes were needed.
